findings.text: The opening sentence renders the EDDB starttime with a trailing 'Z' -- 'E100356 (start 2023-08-07T17:33:25.221Z)' and 'E100353 (start 2021-03-09T21:22:28.631Z)' (lines 15-16) -- which asserts UTC. The source field carries no timezone: eddbreadShot returns a naive YYYYMMDDhhmmss.sss string (op2-shotlist.out line 2 '20210113173923.000'), and the fragment's own table drops the Z. JT-60SA EDDB times are Naka local time (JST), so a reader taking the Z as UTC would misplace each pulse by nine hours. The date ordering and the 880-day gap are unaffected; only the absolute instants are overstated.

The claim 'The only 2026 records in the catalogue are six C-series shots' (line 103) is asserted for the whole catalogue, but the broad all-series enumeration did not run: eddbreadShot('A000000','Z999999') was refused (op2-newest.out: ok=False count=0 irc=1152), so the catalogue was enumerated only for the E series (E100000-E200000, op2-shotlist.out) and the C series (C000000-C200000, op2-cseries.out). The statement is established for those two series and no series was found post-2023 there, but it is not established across every series letter. It does not affect the E-series boundary the node was asked for.

follow_ons.text: The node's own goal text dates the gap 'between the 2023 OP1 campaign and the 2026 OP2 campaign', but its explicit anchors (E101154/E101173 are OP2; E100001 is an old pulse) place OP2 in the 2023 E-series block. EDDB exposes no campaign field, and its only internal E-series campaign gap is E100353->E100356 (2021-03-09 -> 2023-08-07, 880d 20:10:57); every other inter-shot gap is under 26 days. The node honours the explicit anchors -- last OP1 E100353, first OP2 E100356 -- and flags that the date label contradicts them (fragment lines 108-116), recording the alternative boundary E101173->C060028 (2023-12-15 -> 2026-06-24) if the facility's OP-1(2023)/OP-2(2026) naming is meant. This needs coordinator or facility adjudication; EDDB cannot settle it. No repair is possible without a campaign source EDDB does not carry.

The node goal is to establish the first JT-60SA OP2 pulse from EDDB's own shot records; the node does exactly that -- it reads the E-series shot catalogue through eddbreadShot (op2-shotlist.out, count=1167 irc=0) and names the last OP1 pulse E100353 (2021-03-09T21:22:28.631) and the first OP2 pulse E100356 (2023-08-07T17:33:25.221), the only 880-day gap in the series separating a 352-shot 2021 block from an 815-shot 2023 block. The node implements the goal faithfully: from EDDB's own shot catalogue it names last OP1 E100353 (2021-03-09T21:22:28.631) and first OP2 E100356 (2023-08-07T17:33:25.221), the two blocks either side the only large gap in the E-series, and every date, count and gap in the fragment this review re-derived from the retained op2-shotlist.out.
